exact_text:
SMAs tend to act as barriers to price,
putting a stop to any trend that runs into it.
added_conditions: price tends to revert to the consensus (moving average) like a magnet

exact_text:
Stochastics gives a clear buy
signal once it passes below the 20-line (oversold)
and then %K crosses over %D. It gives a clear
sell signal once it passes above the 80-line
(overbought) and then %K crosses under %D.
added_conditions: buy signal requires %K to cross over %D after passing below the 20-line
sell signal requires %K to cross under %D after passing above the 80-line

exact_text:
1. To conﬁrm the validity of current trends and
breakout moves
added_conditions: confirmation requires OBV to move in concert with price, making new highs or lows along with new price highs or lows; when it does not, OBV acts as a contrarian indicator signaling false breakouts

exact_text:
Any breakout from that formation is a tradable
event.
added_conditions: breakout of the upper channel line is expected to develop a new uptrend; breakout of the lower channel line a new downtrend
applies to a narrowing channel or triangle formation

exact_text: It should be on long setups, particularly pullback plays (to be explained later).
added_conditions: bullish weakly trending market
pullbacks tend to be more frequent, steeper, and longer-lived; lengthier pullbacks allow a stop-loss closer to entry and exit targets further away

exact_text:
If price is making a new low, but
the indicators are not making new lows, then you have bullish divergence
added_conditions: applies when evaluating breakdown plays in a bearish strongly trending market; when bullish divergence is present, move on to another chart

exact_text:
the technical indicators we
use (stochastics, CCI, RSI) register overbought and oversold signals that work most robustly in range-bound markets
added_conditions: range-bound (nontrending) market

exact_text:
These three factors register a buy
signal, and the stock is ready to be short-listed
as a valid pullback play.
added_conditions: sharp dip in the stochastics indicator (5,3 period) to or below the oversold 20 line
current candlestick must register a bullish reversal candle of some kind (hammer, engulfing, piercing, or doji)
a bearish candle (close lower than open) results in a wait-and-see condition
setup occurs most often in bullish weakly trending markets that have suffered a short period of price consolidation or profit taking

exact_text:
A break of the trendline drawn
over the tops of this coil marks the buy signal.
added_conditions: coiled spring must last at least seven but no more than 20 trading days
no part of the coil may extend to or beyond the 50 MA
a close below the lower trendline negates the coiled spring

exact_text:
coiled spring is strung out, the higher it will rise after
the spring has sprung
added_conditions: coiled springs longer than 20 days in duration indicate indecision on the part of investors and are best avoided

exact_text:
The last price low corresponds with a higher
low in two or more of the following technical
indicators: MACD, MACD histogram, stochastics, RSI, OBV, and CCI
added_conditions: price makes a lower (last) low
two or more of MACD, MACD histogram, stochastics, RSI, OBV, and CCI register a higher low
a higher low corresponding with the 200 MA, trendline support, or prior price support is preferred
buy signal triggered when a bullish candle (doji, hammer, engulfing, morning star, etc.) is printed on the daily chart

exact_text:
lower price low coupled with three cases of bullish
divergence in the indicators: MACD, RSI, and CCI
added_conditions: setup follows a blow-off double bottom
a bullish candlestick (hammer) marks the second low on the day prior to entry
